cohort: 340 pregnant women in their first trimester with a BMI > 30, no underlying diseases (diabetes, hypertension, kidney, liver, cardiovascular disease), no history of metformin allergy, and a singleton pregnancy, recruited from the gynecology clinic of Motahhari hospital in Urmia.
finding: Prophylactic metformin use in obese pregnant women did not significantly reduce the incidence of gestational diabetes but did result in lower maternal weight gain, reduced birth weight, and lower insulin doses in mothers who developed gestational diabetes.
